market.summary: Indian stocks bounced after four losing sessions, and mid and small caps did better than the Nifty, which helps the small and mid-cap trades (SEJALLTD, THELEELA, TIPSMUSIC). The risks have not gone away: Brent is still near $114 because of Middle East supply fears, the rupee is at a record low and foreign investors are still net sellers over five days. The screener's market regime is still RISK-OFF, so one up day is not a turn.

points.text: Nifty 50 closed at 22,753.20 (+0.68%) and Sensex at 73,606.75 (+0.66%), ending a four-day fall; last week the Nifty lost 2.36%.
Nifty Midcap rose 1.2% and Smallcap 1.4%; 2,262 shares rose and 1,895 fell. Metals (+2.2%) and pharma (+1.8%) led; FMCG, media and consumer durables fell.
Brent was about $114.50, off a near six-month high of $117; the rupee closed 25 paise weaker at 95.19 to the dollar.
NSE provisional flows: FIIs bought ₹888 Cr on 23 Oct but sold a net ₹1,531 Cr over the last five sessions; DIIs bought ₹7,281 Cr over the same five days.

market.watch: Whether mid caps follow through tomorrow; Brent above $117 or the rupee past 95.5 would put pressure back on the market.

HCLTECH.summary: HCLTech filed two press releases today: a semiconductor engineering partnership with Japan's Rapidus and a climate grant programme. Neither gives a deal value, so neither changes the earnings picture. The stock closed at 1,417 (-0.4%) while the IT index rose about 0.5%, so the trade stays at about +0.8R with plenty of room above the stop.

points.text: Rapidus partnership: two HCLTech centres in Bengaluru and Hubli will do chip mask design, process design kits, design-technology co-optimisation and layout work for Rapidus' 2 nm programme; the financial value and headcount were not disclosed.
HCLTech closed at ₹1,417 (-0.37%); IT stocks rose about 0.5% after Friday's fall in US-listed peers (Accenture -3.6%, Cognizant -4.3% on 23 Oct).

HCLTECH.watch: A close above 1,437.78 (+1R) moves the stop to cost; the stop is 1,225.82.

GROWW.summary: No new filing or company news today. Groww closed at 184.48, its second close below the 188.75 stop, so the plan's exit stands even though capital-market stocks rose (BSE +4%). The trade is still marked open in positions.json.

points.text: Close ₹184.48 vs stop ₹188.75 and entry ₹200.80: about -1.35R.
BSE Ltd was among the Nifty's top gainers today (+4%), so the market for brokers was not the problem.

GROWW.watch: The plan says exit. Tell Claude your exit price so the trade can be marked CLOSED.

SEJALLTD.summary: There was no new filing or news. The stock rose to 883.80 from 845.45 as small caps bounced, so the starter is back above its 879.95 entry and well clear of the 838.03 stop. This is market relief, not a company event.

points.text: Close ₹883.80 (+4.5%) on light volume (0.56x the 20-day average); the Nifty Smallcap index rose 1.4%.

SEJALLTD.watch: Add the remaining two-thirds only above 879.95 with confirmation; a close below 838.03 is the exit.

THELEELA.summary: ITC Hotels' results today were strong (revenue +26%, profit +51%, room rates and occupancy both up), which supports Leela's own strong quarter and the view that luxury hotel demand is good. Leela closed at 582.95, back above its 579.15 result-day low and the 573.36 stop, but still below the 604.51 entry.

points.text: ITC Hotels Q2 FY27: revenue ₹1,054 Cr (+26%), PAT ₹201 Cr (+51%), EBITDA margin 32% (+263 bps), occupancy 76% (+481 bps), room rate +14%, RevPAR +21%; the shares rose up to 8%.
Leela closed at ₹582.95 (+0.9%); the screener shows accumulation (7 accumulation vs 2 distribution days in 25 sessions).

THELEELA.watch: A close below 573.36 is the exit; a move back above 604.51 puts the trade in profit.

INDHOTEL.summary: Indian Hotels closed at 795.50, a new post-result closing high and above the 794.75 level from this morning's note, which confirms the drift. ITC Hotels' strong quarter adds to the sector's good results. There was no new IHCL filing.

points.text: Close ₹795.50 at the top of the day's range (99.5%) on 1.1x volume; +0.2R from the ₹785.83 entry.
ITC Hotels: RevPAR +21%, occupancy 76%, and it cited healthy demand and strong MICE business in key markets.

INDHOTEL.watch: +1R is 831.19 (then the stop goes to cost); the stop is 740.47.

TIPSMUSIC.summary: This is a new trade, so this note covers the Q2 call: growth was volume-led with no one-offs, and management expects FY27 growth above its 20% guidance. The risks are concentration (the Warner tie-up is 25-30% of revenue and is up for renewal in September next year), an unsigned YouTube Shorts deal and an open CEO search. The stock closed at 716.90, 1.5% under the 727.89 entry, with the stop well below at 662.11.

points.text: Q2 FY27: revenue about ₹120 Cr (+35% YoY), operating EBITDA ₹84.6 Cr (+25%, 70.5% margin), PAT ₹55.5 Cr (+23%); interim dividend ₹6.50 and a ₹44 Cr buyback completed.
FY27 content spend stays at ₹90-100 Cr (₹71 Cr already spent in H1), so H2 costs should be lighter; about 85% of revenue comes from catalogue more than three years old.

TIPSMUSIC.watch: Wide stop (9% risk): 662.11; +1R 793.67. News on a YouTube Shorts deal would be a catalyst.
